chapter: Trent's band: Texas, St. Louis and the road east
title: Who played with Trent: the Plantation job for Jeter and Pillars and Harry Edison
summary: Mosley got the St. Louis Plantation job for Jeter and Pillars, with Claude Hopkins's help, and took Harry Edison down with him.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: I don't think he played with Trini, he played with the little band that you had in Cleveland; he never played with Trini, I don't think.
I asked Pillars the same thing and he said no, he never played with him, he played with the band, the seven piece band at the Majestic and all over the place.
That's the reason I had to review my thinking, because I was trying to remember--

I remember reading that and I always wanted to ask him. He would have been just about the age enough to play with the band before it broke up; I did all the reading and stuff and I never saw anything about that, and you know me, I'm forever into research.
But I saw on one of the questions, (inaudible)
But he couldn't have been--
He was there--he was with Jeter and Pillars in St. Louis.

But I got that job for them, for Jeter and Pillars. You know, Claude Hopkins had just left St. Louis and these guys at the Plantation asked Claude to look for a group for them, and when Claude heard me, and I had made arrangements to join his band later in Chicago, because I told him that I wanted to go down to St. Louis with Jeter and Pillars to help them hold that job--
You were going to open up for them?
I opened with them, and Harry Edison--
Harry Edison was in the band?
Yeah, he went down. We stopped by Harry's mother--he's from Ohio anyway, and we stopped by and she was telling me to take care of her baby, and there I was, I wasn't much older than he.
Right.
We were just about the same age.
I had to revise my thinking too, because I said--no, I don't think Harry was in that band when we broke up in Albany.
I know he got his reputation Jeter and Pillars, he stayed down there until he came up and then he got with Basie right after that.
(Inaudible).
We're getting ahead of what we want.
I'm sorry.
No, no, it's not your fault. It doesn't really matter that much.
